casual_social.description: Default Quebec B2C — joual, English-influenced, distinctive vocabulary.

professional_casual.description: Montreal/Quebec LinkedIn — cleaner French, light joual.

corporate_formal.description: Government, banking — closer to international French.

grammar_quirks: Heavy English borrowing despite French-protection laws
Religious-origin vulgarities (sacres) used as expletives — culturally specific
Tu vs vous less strict than France

code_switching_patterns.english_in_french: Heavy historical English borrowing — chum, blonde, char, checker, parking
rules: Quebec brands prefer Quebec-French over France-French to signal local identity
Bill 96 / language laws — official communication must be French-first

do_not_use: Sacres (tabarnak, câlisse) in commercial work — culturally inappropriate
Anglicisms that signal lazy translation rather than authentic Quebec speech

quebec_city: More traditional, conservative, proud Francophone identity

example_translations.note: 'L'fun' is the Quebec native marker for 'fun' — ubiquitous.
